newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Regional currency woes hit Singapore stock market.
newsitem.headline: Regional currency woes hit Singapore stock market.

text.p: The bears in the regional currency market infiltrated the Singapore stock market on Wednesday, sending most shares lower, dealers said.
"The market is reacting to the regional currency blues. There is devaluation paranoia, especially in the ringgit and peso, following the baht float," said a local dealer.
"Also, what is happening in Cambodia is seen as destablising for the region," he said.
Profit-taking by funds following recent gains further dampened sentiment.
"Funds were taking profit since the market has risen quite a bit this week, with some stocks rising over 10 percent in two days," said an analyst with a Singapore brokerage.
The Straits Times Industrials Index fell 24.26 points or 1.21 percent to end at 1,982.97. Helping drag it down was soft drink firm Fraser & Neave, which fell 50 cents to end at Singapore $10.20.
The SES electronics index, which held its ground for most of the day, eased 0.18 to end at 129.21. It was underpinned by Creative Technology and Flextech Holdings.
"Certain electronic stocks remain a buy because of their fundamentals. These companies have the potential for 20-25 percent earnings growth," said a broker.
Property stocks took a beating, driving the index down 18.54 points to 689.79 on renewed concerns of further downside for Singapore residential properties.
Drug firm Tianjin Zhongxin led the actives with over 7.8 million shares. It rose a cent to US$1.14 on continued buy recommendations by research houses.
Losers included foreign tranches of Singapore Press Holdings and banks, which rose sharply earlier in the week.
